title: Double particles: には, にも, とは and の + particle
summary: There is no such thing as a combined particle. Logical and non-logical particles can sit together; two logical particles cannot.

blocks.text: Lists of "particle combinations" make you memorize which can pair with which. You do not need them. Every particle just does its own job. Two facts explain all the pairings.

The five main **logical** particles are **が, を, に, で, へ**. They say what role each noun plays in the sentence: who does it, what it is done to, where, to what. A noun has one role, so **two logical particles cannot stand together**. The **non-logical** particles **は** and **も** do not give a role; they only make a topic or sub-topic. They fit beside a logical particle with no clash.

**が** (main carriage) and **を** (direct object) are so basic that nothing can be put next to them. To make such a noun a topic, **drop** the particle and put は or も alone. さくらをなぐった becomes さくらはなぐった, and the missing を is understood. You never see をは or がは.

rows: 冬には雪が降る (in winter, at least)
春にも雪が降る (in spring too)
topic and contrast at a place

blocks.text: In 明日学校に行く, に is needed to show the destination. 明日学校には行く says "as for school, I will go (but maybe not somewhere else)". 明日学校にも行く says "I will go to school too". The logical particle gives the role, and は or も adds a feeling.
The **nominalizing の** turns whatever comes before it into a noun, and a noun can take any logical particle: 泳ぐのが好きだ, 泳ぐのを見た, 泳ぐのに疲れた.

blocks.jp: この町にも図書館がある。
blocks.en: This town has a library as well.

blocks.jp: 友達と一緒に走るのが楽しい。
blocks.en: Running together with a friend is fun.

items: Logical: **が を に で へ**. Non-logical: **は も**.
Two logical particles never combine; a logical plus は or も does.
**が** and **を** drop away when は or も takes over.
**の** (the noun box) can be followed by any logical particle.

questions.instruction: Which pair is made up of logical particles only?
questions.note: が, を, に, で, へ are logical; は and も are not.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap for "in spring as well"
questions.note: に gives time, も adds "also".

questions.instruction: Why can you not say さくらをはなぐった?
options: を cannot be combined; use は alone
questions.note: The direct particles drop away when は takes over.

options: 彼がはよく知っている。
彼にがよく知っている。
彼をはよく知っている。
questions.note: が is replaced by は.

questions.prompt: に and で can be written together as にで to make a place particle.
questions.note: Two logical particles clash: a noun has one role.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun that is both a topic and a place
questions.note: で marks the place; は makes it a topic.

questions.instruction: Which meaning does 学校には行く suggest?
options: (I) will go to school, even if not elsewhere

questions.instruction: Which meaning does 学校にも行く suggest?
options: (I) will go to school, in addition to elsewhere

questions.instruction: Why can の take any logical particle?
options: It turns the clause into a noun
questions.note: A noun can take any role marker.
The boxed clause 海で泳ぐの takes が, then the engine.

questions.instruction: In 冬には雪だるまを作る, what does は add?
options: Winter becomes a topic set against other seasons
questions.note: に gives the time; は makes the topic and contrast.
